annotations.text:
IRC, an app for vibeee, after XChat Cerulean.
Binary echat, readable name IRC. Lives in apps/, not the system tree.
Slate theme throughout, the toolkit's own rail on the left, Ark Mono for what was said and Ark Pixel for the chrome. 800x480, the whole screen.

The rail
The same control Settings uses: 124 wide, 26 tall rows, the chosen one a filled band and the rest plain text on the sunken ground, with a caption at the foot where Settings puts the version and this puts your nickname.

It needs two things it does not have. A row held under another, so channels sit beneath their network. And a count, so a rail row can say how much is waiting. Both are general: any rail with more places than fit wants them.

The transcript
A run of messages from one person carries their name once, and the words run the full width of the pane rather than beside a column of names repeated down the screen. On 800 pixels that column was costing 88 of them on every line.

What is kept from IRC: the server speaks with a dash rather than a name, a line that names you takes the ground a chosen row takes, and ops and voice are marked in the list of who is here.

Underneath it is a scrolling pane of wrapped lines, which the toolkit already draws.

About the nick colours
Cerulean tells names apart by hue. The theme carries one highlight and no palette to draw seven from, so this leans on the grouping instead: one bold name per run, yours in the accent.

If you want the hues, they belong in the theme as a named palette every app can reach, not invented in this one.

Networks
The directory XChat has, in this system's shape: a list with the chosen one's settings on a row beneath it, the way the network pane puts an interface's settings under its list.

Connect is the primary action and carries the accent, as Save and Join do.
